records.summary: •During busy hours, slums are filled with people going about their business or looking for trouble. Movement counts as difficult terrain. •At night, the alleys clear but become more dangerous as thieves, gangs, and predators emerge from the shadows. 3.Escape Routes: •Chase scenes through slums are common. Players must succeed on a series of Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks (DC 12–15) to climb walls, jump over obstacles, and navigate narrow alleys. Creative players may use the environment to escape—tipping crates, hiding in trash, or using rooftops.

•Using public transit systems like bullet trains or taxis is the fastest way to travel—but these services can be monitored. Players risk being tracked by corporations or government agents. •Rush hour and protests create bottlenecks. If players travel by vehicle, Dexterity (Vehicle Handling) checks (DC 15) may be required to avoid accidents.

•Some merchants sell faulty goods. A Wisdom (Insight) check (DC 13) is required to spot counterfeit or cursed items before purchasing them. Failure results in a useless or cursed item being purchased.
•Every NPC may know bits of information or rumors. A successful Charisma (Persuasion) or Charisma (Deception) check (DC 12) allows the players to extract valuable knowledge or misinformation.

•Wind Gusts: Strong winds can cause tents to collapse. Characters must make Strength saving throws (DC 12) to secure structures during windstorms. •Rain and Mud: Heavy rain turns the camp into a muddy mess, making movement difficult and doubling exhaustion recovery time. •Desert Heat or Snow: Extreme temperatures require Constitution saves (DC 13) each hour or impose exhaustion until characters find shade or warmth.
•For camps with pack animals, players must make Animal Handling checks (DC 13) to keep animals calm and avoid injury when navigating through difficult terrain.

•Disputes over prices, rival vendors, or rowdy patrons can lead to spontaneous fights. Players caught in the middle must either join in or avoid the fight with Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks (DC 12). 4.Black Market Risks: •Buying illegal goods risks detection by guards or rival gangs. Each transaction involves a stealth roll (DC 14). A failure might result in an encounter with the authorities or a rival faction ambush.

•The chaotic market separates one party member or NPC from the group. The players must search the market or question vendors (Investigation DC 12) to reunite with them. 4.Unexpected Auction: •The party stumbles upon an auction of rare goods or magical items. Competing buyers include nobles, merchants, and criminals. Players may need to outbid others or sabotage rivals. 5.Theft in Progress: •A thief steals an item from a vendor or NPC, and the party witnesses it. They can pursue the thief (Dexterity checks DC 14) or negotiate with them afterward to recover the stolen goods.

•Adventurers trying to avoid the streets can move across rooftops. A series of Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks (DC 14) allows them to run, jump, and slide across buildings. Failure may result in a fall (1d6 damage per 10 feet) or getting cornered by rooftop guards.

•Entering gang-controlled territory risks ambushes. Players may need to negotiate, bribe, or fight their way through. A failed Charisma (Persuasion) or (Intimidation) check (DC 13) triggers combat. 4.Augmentation Failure: •Cybernetic implants may malfunction due to power surges or sabotage. Players with augmentations must make Constitution saves (DC 12) or suffer temporary penalties to physical or mental abilities.
•Corporate facilities hide security measures such as trap doors and concealed turrets. A failed Perception check (DC 14) results in triggering these defenses.

Animals, if not cared for, suffer fatigue and movement speed penalties. Characters can use Animal Handling checks (DC 12) to tend to animals, ensuring theyʼre fed, watered, and rested.

1.Limited Supplies: Resources are scarce. Each day, roll a d6 to determine if the camp is running low on essentials (food, water, or medicine). On a 1 or 2, the group suffers shortages, increasing the need for foraging or hunting. 2.Predator Attacks: Predators or scavengers may approach the camp at night, attracted by the scent of food or livestock. Spotting them in time requires a Wisdom (Perception) check (DC 14). Failure may result in livestock losses or player injury. 3.Disease and Illness: Close quarters and poor hygiene can lead to illness. Once a week, players must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 12). Failure results in temporary fatigue, imposing -1 to Strength and Dexterity until a long rest. 4.Fire Hazard: Due to the flammable materials used, fire can spread quickly in the camp. Any open flame or fire spells near tents require a Dexterity check (DC 13) to prevent an outbreak, which could cause 1d6 fire damage per round until extinguished.

1.Pickpockets: Characters passing through markets or crowded areas must succeed on a Wisdom (Perception) check (DC 14) to spot a pickpocket. On failure, they lose a small item or a portion of their gold. 2.Accidents: •Collapsing Balconies: Dexterity saving throw (DC 15) to avoid 3d6 bludgeoning damage. •Runaway Carriage: A failed check results in the character being knocked prone and taking 2d8 bludgeoning damage. 3.Diseases: •Urban Blight: A contagious disease that spreads through contact in the slums, requiring a Constitution saving throw (DC 12) to avoid infection. Infected characters lose 1 HP every hour until treated. •Airborne Fever: Smog can carry pathogens, forcing a Constitution save (DC 13) every day. Failure results in exhaustion that worsens until cured. 4.Crime and Corruption: •Bribery or Blackmail: NPCs may require bribes to cooperate. Avoiding blackmail schemes involves opposed Charisma (Deception) or Intelligence (Investigation) rolls. •False Arrest: Players may encounter crooked guards framing them for crimes. A Charisma (Persuasion) check (DC 16) can convince the authorities of their innocence.

1.Corporate Heist: •The players are hired to infiltrate a corporation and steal critical data. They must bypass security, deal with drones, and escape before reinforcements arrive. 2.Gang Raid: •A gang attacks a rivalʼs headquarters, and the players are caught in the crossfire. They must decide whether to join one side, escape, or negotiate for safe passage. 3.AI Gone Rogue: •An AI running part of the cityʼs infrastructure becomes self-aware and unpredictable. The players must find a way to shut it down or make a deal with it before chaos spreads. 4.Augmentation Sabotage: •The playersʼ cybernetic implants are hacked, limiting their abilities or forcing them to follow strange directives. They must seek out the hacker or find a countermeasure. 5.Underground Tournament: •A secret arena hosts illegal augmented combat matches. The players can compete for prizes, but winning may attract dangerous attention. 6.Virtual Reality Prison: •A rival faction traps the players in a virtual simulation, where they must navigate puzzles and combat scenarios to escape before their bodies deteriorate in the real world.

1.Terrain Types: •Cramped Alleys: Narrow spaces between buildings make movement difficult. Characters must move single file, and melee combat is restricted to tight quarters. •Makeshift Paths: Wooden planks or old debris form unstable bridges over gutters or canals. Characters crossing these paths must make a Dexterity (Acrobatics) check (DC 12) to avoid falling. •Flooded Alleys: Poor drainage leaves some alleys knee-deep in murky water. Moving through flooded alleys counts as difficult terrain, and any creature moving through the water must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 13) to avoid contracting disease. •Abandoned Buildings: Dilapidated homes provide cover and hiding spots. However, they may collapse with sudden movement (Strength save DC 14 to avoid being trapped). 2.Weather and Conditions: •

Long rests require finding a secure safehouse. Renting a hotel room or hacking into an unoccupied apartment provides temporary refuge, but rival hackers or drones may still locate the players if theyʼre not careful.

1.Navigating the Maze: •The alleyways twist and turn unpredictably. A successful Intelligence (Investigation) or Wisdom (Survival) check (DC 15) is required every 30 minutes to avoid getting lost. Failure means wandering into a dead end or dangerous area.

1.Seagulls: •Loud and annoying, these birds steal food and valuables, forcing players to make Dexterity saving throws (DC 10) to keep their belongings. 2.Rats: •Found in both taverns and cargo holds. They carry disease, forcing Constitution saves (DC 13) if bitten. 3.Exotic Marine Life: •Occasionally, strange fish or sea creatures are sold in the market—or escape their pens, causing chaos in the streets.

1.Unstable Docks: •Old wooden docks may give way under pressure. A Dexterity saving throw (DC 14) is required to avoid falling into the water (and possibly encountering underwater hazards). 2.Loose Cargo: •Crates and barrels might fall off carts or ships, blocking pathways or causing injuries. A Dexterity saving throw (DC 12) avoids 2d6 bludgeoning damage. 3.Storm Surge: •If a storm strikes, the harbor may flood. Characters must make a Strength (Athletics) check (DC 15) to avoid being swept into the water. 4.Disease and Contamination: •Port cities are prone to outbreaks. Characters interacting with sick individuals must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC 13) or risk infection. An infected character suffers 1 point of exhaustion each day until cured.

•Short Rest: The inn or tavern offers basic comfort. A short rest here restores the normal amount of HP, and players may overhear gossip while they rest. •Long Rest: Long rests are usually peaceful, though loud or unruly behavior might get the players kicked out of their lodging. Sleeping outside carries the risk of exposure or encounters with wild animals. •Interrupted Rest: Events such as fires, robberies, or night raids may disrupt rest at the GMʼs discretion. On a roll of 5 or lower on a d20, something disturbs the rest.

•Short Rest: Dockside taverns offer cheap food and drink. However, resting in a seedy establishment may lead to theft. Characters must succeed on a Wisdom (Perception) check (DC 12) to avoid waking up robbed. •Long Rest: Luxury inns in the merchant district provide a peaceful nightʼs sleep, granting +1 temporary HP upon waking. Characters resting on a ship must deal with cramped quarters and rolling seas, risking one level of exhaustion if they fail a Constitution saving throw (DC 14).
Short rests are possible in quiet corners, though players must remain alert for thieves. On a roll of 5 or lower on a d20, an encounter occurs—such as a pickpocket or street brawl.

1.Court Intrigue: •Characters attending high-society events must succeed on Charisma (Deception) or Intelligence (Politics) checks (DC 16) to avoid offending influential NPCs. •Failing a social interaction could lead to scandal or losing valuable allies. 2.Merchant Deals: Players negotiating prices or trade deals must roll contested Charisma (Persuasion) or Intelligence (Economics) checks. A failed negotiation could result in higher prices or losing access to goods entirely. 3.Legal Trouble: •If arrested, players can either escape, bribe, or appeal in court. The appeal requires a successful Charisma (Persuasion) check (DC 18) with a lawyerʼs assistance. Escaping triggers a city-wide manhunt.
1.Hacked Implants: •Players with cybernetic augmentations must make Wisdom saves (DC 15) to resist being hijacked by a malicious hacker. Failure results in the loss of control over the implant.

•A union hall is bombed, and players must track whether it was a false-flag by the Coalition or an inside betrayal. •The Glowworm Triad is dealing a mutagenic variant of emberstone thatʼs causing miners to go berserk underground. •A Steamwrights' strike forces the players to jury-rig factory equipment to prevent a massive explosion. •A sentient furnace awakens in an old war foundry, whispering secrets of the pre-imperial age. •A ghost crew of long-dead workers begins haunting the night shift, and players are hired to investigate—or cover it up.

records.summary: •Can reroll a failed Athletics or Acrobatics check once per long rest in the Jungle
•Gain +1 to rolls involving physical labor, endurance, or machinery. •You can reroll one failed save vs. poison, smoke, or industrial fumes per rest.
•You can identify an industrial device or machineʼs make and era with a DC 10 Insight check. •Once per session, you can shrug off a fire-based hazard or effect as if it dealt half damage.

•You are immune to exhaustion caused by crowds, heat, or light pollution •Once per long rest, you may reroll a failed check when coordinating a group task or operation 🌀 Themes & Tone •Fluid identity: Midbay absorbs influences without losing its sense of self. •Everyday heroism: Locals solve problems before institutions even hear about them. •Dynamic neutrality: The region is politically calm—but underneath, deals are always happening.
